paper_sections.title: Promoter haplotypes of interleukin-10 gene linked to cortex plasticity in subjects with risk of Alzheimer's disease
Statistical analysis involving demographic and neuropsychological data

description.value: The study examined whether IL-10 promoter ATA haplotype status and amnestic mild cognitive impairment are associated with differences in bilateral hippocampal functional connectivity and whether connectivity relates to memory performance.

design.value: A cross-sectional 2 × 2 factorial study compared amnestic mild cognitive impairment subjects and healthy controls according to IL-10 promoter ATA haplotype status using resting-state functional MRI, with voxel-wise hippocampal functional connectivity and neuropsychological assessments.

inclusion_criteria.value: subjective memory impairment corroborated by subject and an informant

no or minimal impairment in activities of daily living

modality.value: conventional axial Fast Relaxation Fast Spin Echo sequence T2 weighted anatomic MR images

instrument.value: General Electric 1.5 Tesla scanner (General Electric Medical Systems, USA) with a homogeneous birdcage head coil

description.value: Conventional axial T2-weighted images were obtained to rule out major white matter changes, cerebral infarction or other lesions; TR = 3500 ms; TE = 103 ms; FA = 90°; acquisition matrix = 320 × 192; FOV = 240 mm × 240 mm; thickness = 6.0 mm; gap = 0 mm; NEX = 2.0.

instrument.value: General Electric 1.5 Tesla scanner (General Electric Medical Systems, USA) with a homogeneous birdcage head coil

description.value: High-resolution T1-weighted axial images covering the whole brain were acquired using a 3D spoiled gradient echo sequence; TR = 9.9 ms; TE = 2.1 ms; FA = 15°; acquisition matrix = 256 × 192; FOV = 240 mm × 240 mm; thickness = 2.0 mm; gap = 0 mm.

instrument.value: General Electric 1.5 Tesla scanner (General Electric Medical Systems, USA) with a homogeneous birdcage head coil

description.value: 30 contiguous axial slices using a GRE-EPI pulse sequence; TR = 3000 ms; TE = 40 ms; FA = 90°; acquisition matrix = 64 × 64; FOV = 240 × 240 mm; thickness = 4.0 mm; gap = 0 mm; 3.75 × 3.75 mm in-plane resolution parallel to the anterior commissure–posterior commissure line. The sequence generated 142 volumes in 7 min and 6 s.

The first eight volumes were discarded for T1 equilibration; remaining images were corrected for timing differences and motion effects, spatially normalized into the SPM5 Montreal Neurological Institute echo-planar imaging template with resampling to 3 × 3 × 3 mm3 voxels, smoothed with an 8 × 8 × 8 mm3 Gaussian kernel, detrended and temporally bandpass filtered at 0.01–0.08 Hz.

steps.value: corrected for timing differences and motion effects
excluded participants with head motion >3 mm maximum displacement along any axis or 3° angular motion
spatially normalized into the SPM5 Montreal Neurological Institute echo-planar imaging template
smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of 8 × 8 × 8 mm3
removed the linear trend of time courses

model_settings.value: Bilateral hippocampus was used as the ROI; mean ROI time series was correlated with every voxel time series; Fisher's z-transform was applied; six head motion parameters and mean global, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals were introduced as covariates; voxelwise-based grey matter volume correction was applied.

level.value: subject-level maps followed by group-level analysis

model_settings.value: 2 × 2 ANOVA with groups (aMCI and controls) and haplotypes (without ATA haplotype and with ATA haplotype); corrected p < 0.05 by Monte Carlo simulation, single voxel p = 0.05, minimum cluster size 10,503 mm3, FWHM = 8 mm, with mask.
Group comparisons of the mean functional connectivity value within the mask of ANOVA interactions; statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
Correlation between neuropsychological test scores and the mean value of functional connectivity within the mask of ANOVA interactions; statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

model_type.value: nonparametric Mann–Whitney U tests, independent samples t-tests and Chi-square test

model_settings.value: Mann–Whitney U tests and independent samples t-tests were used for demographic and neuropsychological group comparisons; Chi-square test was used to explore gender differences; statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
